chunks: Abu Shakir al-Daysani said, 'In the Quran there is a verse that supports our claim.' I asked, 'What is it?'
He said, '[It is:] "And He is the one who is God in the heaven and God on earth."' [43:84]
I did not know how to answer him. So I performed hajj and informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said, 'This is the speech of a wicked zindiq. When you return to him say: "What is your name in al-Kufa?" He will say so-and-so. Say: "What is your name in al-Basra?" He will say so-and-so. Then say: Likewise, God our Lord — in the heaven He is God, on earth He is God, in the seas He is God, in the deserts He is God, and in every place He is God.'
He (the narrator) said: I returned and came to Abu Shakir and informed him. He said, 'This was brought from al-Hijaz.'

key_terms.إِلَهٌ: ilah — deity, object of worship; used here to assert God's unique sovereignty in every realm
key_terms.الْقِفَارِ: deserts/wastelands — barren uninhabited lands, underscoring God's omnipresence
key_terms.زِنْدِيقٍ: zindiq — a heretic/dualist, specifically a Manichaean who denies divine unity

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say in response to Abu Shakir al-Daysani's claim that Quran 43:84 supports the existence of multiple gods?
ai.summary: Hisham ibn al-Hakam narrates a theological debate with Abu Shakir al-Daysani, a Manichaean dualist who attempted to use Quran 43:84 to argue for polytheism. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes him with a brilliant analogy: just as a person retains the same identity in different cities, God is the one deity in every realm — heaven, earth, seas, deserts, and all places. Abu Shakir's remark that 'this was brought from al-Hijaz' implicitly concedes the force of the argument.

en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following. “Abu Shakir al-Daysani said, ‘In the Quran there is a verse that says what we say.’ I asked, “What is that?”
He replied, “ It is God who is the Lord of the heavens and is the Lord on earth. He is All-wise and All-knowing [43:84].”
I did not know the answer? During Hajj I mentioned it to Imam abu ‘Abdallah who said this.

“This is the statement of a wicked atheist. When you go back say to him, ‘What is your name in Basra? He will say so and so. Ask, “What is your name in al-Kufah? He will say so and so. Say in the same way is our Lord in the heavens. He is the king in the heavens and the Lord on earth. He is the Lord in oceans and on land and in all places. “
The narrator has said, “I came back, went to abu Shakir and explained to him the answer. He said, “This (answer) is brought from al- Hijaz.”
